findings.title: design.md Risks/Trade-offs row 193 (`.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` cascade ambiguity) is residue from the pre-Option-D framing
findings.recommendation: Remove or rewrite the SKILL.md ambiguity risk row. Under D7's Option D (lifecycle-invariant OUT list only; no file-extension discrimination), there is no SKILL.md ambiguity — `.claude/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` is IN unless inside an OUT category (it isn't), so cascade applies uniformly. The row's mitigation language (`Spec'd as case-by-case evaluation against the project-level-governing-docs umbrella`) describes a pre-Option-D mechanism that the spec body no longer specifies. Two resolution paths: (a) delete the row entirely (the Option D framing eliminates the risk); (b) replace it with the genuinely-remaining risk under Option D, e.g., 'Cascade applies to framework files when developing orbit itself' — mitigated by the dedicated 'Cascade applies to orbit framework files when developing orbit itself' scenario in the spec. Path (a) is cleaner.

findings.title: design.md Risks/Trade-offs row 192 contradicts the v1↔v2 migration framing in the spec body (`semantically equivalent` vs `NOT bijective`)
findings.recommendation: Update the row's mitigation language. The current text states `old ripple_flagged_files_aggregate field is replaced by ripple_cascade.flagged_not_applied[] (semantically equivalent)`, which contradicts the spec body at specs/orbit-address-reviews/spec.md:234 (`The shapes are NOT bijective — v1 archived JSONs cannot be losslessly upconverted to v2`). The W2-iter1 resolution explicitly reframed v1→v2 as a structural change (per-resolution attribution gained in v2; lost reading v1). The design.md row should match: replace `semantically equivalent` with `structural change (v2 captures per-resolution attribution; v1's top-level aggregate had none)`. Optional: also drop the `Reader-side migration handled by orbit-status's tier-1 best-effort parse` sentence (orbit-status capability doesn't exist in baseline or archives — forward-reference; see S2).

findings.title: `recommendation_fork.structured_path_skipped_reason` field referenced in scenarios + tasks but not enumerated in formal field-shape definition
findings.recommendation: Add `structured_path_skipped_reason` to the formal field-shape enumeration for `recommendation_fork` at lines 224-229. Current state: the field appears in the malformed-array fallback scenario at line 213 and in tasks.md task 4.5, but the `Field semantics` block at lines 219-232 (which exhaustively lists the recommendation_fork sub-fields: detected, source, options_presented, chosen, discuss_invoked) omits it. An implementer reading only the field-shape block would not know to emit it. Insert: `- structured_path_skipped_reason: string (present only when the structured path was skipped due to malformed recommendation_options; names the reason — e.g., "only 1 entry in array", "missing label on entry index 2")`. Also update task 5.1's field enumeration to include it.

findings.title: Empirical-evidence references to `bootstrap-orbit-status-cli` archive path that doesn't exist
findings.recommendation: explore.md:134 cites `openspec/changes/archive/2026-05-20-bootstrap-orbit-status-cli/.orbit-runs/review-system-*.json` as empirical evidence backing #14 / #18; design.md:192 references `orbit-status's tier-1 best-effort parse`. Verified: no `bootstrap-orbit-status-cli` directory exists in `openspec/changes/archive/`, and no `orbit-status` capability exists under `openspec/specs/`. These appear to be either user-shorthand for an undocumented experience or forward-references to a future change. Two resolution paths: (a) replace the cited path with the actual archive that exhibits the empirical pattern, OR a footnote acknowledging the evidence is from undocumented dogfooding sessions; (b) drop the specific path citation, retain the qualitative claim (`5 WARNINGs silently dropped in iter-N+1`). Low priority — does not block apply since the evidence is backing rationale, not a normative spec claim. Pre-existing drift; could be tackled separately.

findings.title: tasks.md task 1.4 groups `--no-cascade suppressed` with `OUT-category reason codes` despite spec explicitly distinguishing the two
findings.recommendation: Reword task 1.4 to distinguish OUT-category reasons from mode-suppression. Spec at specs/orbit-address-reviews/spec.md:264 explicitly says `--no-cascade does not classify by IN/OUT — it suppresses cascade entirely; the --no-cascade suppressed reason applies uniformly. Per-OUT-category reasons (audit-trail, baseline-spec, etc.) only appear in the default mode when cascade DID try to apply and was structurally blocked.` Task 1.4 currently lists all 5 reason codes (audit-trail, baseline-spec, cross-change, safe-exclusion, --no-cascade) under the umbrella `OUT-category reason codes used in flagged_not_applied[]` — which conflates a structural classification (4 OUT categories) with a mode toggle. Suggested phrasing: `Document the four OUT-category reason codes (audit-trail, baseline-spec, cross-change, safe-exclusion) AND the mode-suppression reason code (--no-cascade suppressed) used in flagged_not_applied[] entries...`. Trivial doc-clarification.
